Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (CTO - Willowpeak), Ethan Cole (Senior ML Eng), Hannah Lee (Product)

Summary (auto): discuss PLG/self-serve onramp, free credits usage, tradeoffs between Hosted / Dedicated / Private for Willowpeak's latency-sensitive telemetry summarization feature.

[00:00] Sofia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call — this is Sofia from Redwood, AE on the account, and Miguel our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Priya Desai: Hi, Priya here. thanks.
[00:09] Ethan Cole: Ethan.
[00:10] Hannah Lee: Hannah.
[00:12] Miguel Torres: Hey all, Miguel, nice to meet you. we'll try to cover time-to-first-request, credits, and basic hosting fit for your use case.

[00:22] Sofia Chen: Priya, maybe to start, could you give us 60 seconds on what you're trying to build and what success looks like for the next 8 weeks?
[00:30] Priya Desai: Sure, quick version — we're building a real-time telemetry summarization pipeline for our fleet monitoring product. the main constraint is we need sub-200ms p95 for short payloads in the UI, and we also have to satisfy a set of data residency and audit requirements for a subset of customers. team wants a low friction path to evaluate — free credits, quick PoC, try hosted API first if it meets latency.
[00:55] Miguel Torres: got it — sub 200ms p95 is tight for hosted endpoints depending on model choice and sequence length; but for short payloads and smaller models we often can hit that with the right routing and cache/batching settings. can you share typical request size? tokens or bytes?
[01:10] Ethan Cole: Typical payload is 80 to 250 tokens after preproc, most are on the lower side. concurrency will be spiky during paging events — could see 40 to 150 QPS for short bursts.
[01:24] Miguel Torres: that helps. for the PLG/onramp we usually recommend starting with Redwood API hosted because it's fastest to TTFR — you get free credits, SDKs, and we can help with a quick account and sample keys. Dedicated is next if you need predictable throughput or isolation; Private/VPC if you need strict residency or cannot route data off your VPC.

[01:46] Priya Desai: Two quick things: 1) How do credits map to tokens/requests in practice? 2) For the residency/audit customers — how mature is your Private/VPC offering? timeline?
[01:58] Sofia Chen: Good Qs. credits are applied to hosted usage and we send a starter pack — typically enough for a few thousand requests depending on model choice. i'll send a simple calculator but rough rule: for a smaller open model on our catalog you might see X credits per 1k tokens vs a larger LLM costing more. Miguel, want to add on private?
[02:16] Miguel Torres: Private is available as a customer-managed control plane or on-prem option; our VPC private deployments are shipping and we have a few customers in pilot. timeline depends on your security gap analysis — typically a multi-week engagement to provision and network. also note: with Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools and stronger SLOs, which can hit your p95 goals without fully private infra.

[02:44] Hannah Lee: Is there a way to test latency on hosted with our real traffic shape without sending production data? we have privacy constraints for some customers.
[02:54] Miguel Torres: Yes — two options: 1) synthetic replay using your anonymized traces; we can run benchmark scripts from our side or you run via our SDKs. 2) bring a sanitized seed dataset and run a small trial in a restricted environment. both work. Folks sometimes use prefix caching and short-context model variants to mimic production.

[03:14] Ethan Cole: what's the fastest path — we want to see a first token in our app in <2 days if possible.
[03:19] Sofia Chen: For TTFR under 48 hours we recommend self-serve sign-up, apply the starter credits (we'll provision on our side), then follow our quickstart SDK — usually ~15-30 minutes to make the first API call if you have an app dev. Miguel can also run a quick pairing session to help wire up the SDK.
[03:35] Miguel Torres: i'll do a short pairing. we can also pre-configure a small demo project and drop you keys — you'll swap in your client and you're off. i can run the latency profile against your sample payload and share results in a short spreadsheet.

[03:50] Priya Desai: On security: SOC2 is critical for procurement, plus we need SAML SSO for the control plane and customer-level RBAC. also KMS integration for key wrap on private. can you confirm?
[04:02] Sofia Chen: yes — Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we provide SAML/SSO + SCIM for provisioning; RBAC in the console and audit logs are exposed. for Private/VPC we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for encryption at rest. i'll attach the security pack.
[04:18] Hannah Lee: Any gotchas on data retention and logs? we need to ensure we can opt out of data usage for model training.
[04:26] Miguel Torres: Hosted accounts have retention & opt-out controls; by default Redwood does not use customer data to train models unless there's an opt-in program. we also expose per-request audit logs and token-level cost breakdown in the console. small note — some of our older docs say 'Redwood Optima' in places, ignore that — official name is Redwood Optimize, it's our cost/perf toolkit.
[04:48] Priya Desai: Nice. on the cost side, if we start with hosted using the free credits and then decide to reserve Dedicated later, what's the migration path?
[04:57] Sofia Chen: It's pretty smooth — same API surface. you'll be able to pin model versions and change routing policies; Dedicated becomes available as a capacity tier and we can migrate traffic gradually with canaries. the console supports rollouts, fallback policies, and model version control so your app code rarely changes.
[05:14] Ethan Cole: For the p95 target, how much of the gain is infra vs model choice vs software patterns (like prefix caching)?
[05:21] Miguel Torres: It's a mix. infra and kernel selection matter for large models; for short payloads model choice (smaller distilled variants) + prefix/KV cache and batching heuristics normally yield the biggest gains per cost. our serving runtime supports continuous batching and will dynamically adjust but for <200ms p95 you often pick a compact model, tune batching windows, and use a low-latency region.
[05:44] Priya Desai: Do you have any reference for customers that had similar latency/residency mix?
[05:49] Sofia Chen: We have a case—not public—that used Dedicated for a fleet product. i'll share an anonymized benchmark and a short one-pager.

[06:00] Hannah Lee: What about spikes — autoscaling? our traffic pattern is very bursty, we don't want cold starts to add 500ms.
[06:09] Miguel Torres: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity; hosted has warm pools and global routing with capacity fallbacks. if bursts are very short and frequent, we'd recommend Dedicated or provisioning a small reserved pool with burst options.

[06:25] Priya Desai: procurement will ask about SLA and uptime. do you provide formal SLAs on Hosted?
[06:30] Sofia Chen: Hosted has best-effort SLAs for the free tier; production-hosted and Dedicated come with formal SLOs and SLA add-ons for enterprise customers. we'll detail those in the contract proposal.

[06:44] Ethan Cole: Any integrations with our observability stack? we want traces that tie request IDs back to our logs.
[06:50] Miguel Torres: Console exposes per-request trace IDs and we provide tracing hooks and a small agent to push events to your telemetry system. we can instrument with OpenTelemetry and export spans to your backend.

[07:05] Sofia Chen: Ok, quick recap and next steps — Miguel, you're going to run a small benchmark on the sample payload and share results. I'll send pricing + credits guide + security pack. Priya will confirm residency constraints. we also agreed to schedule a 30-min pilot scoping session next week.
[07:20] Priya Desai: Yep that sounds right. can you include the simple credits calculator so procurement can see expected spend?
[07:26] Sofia Chen: Absolutely.
